html:
1What You Will Learn

Note

Acronyms in this note. ML: machine learning; HNSW: Hierarchical Navigable Small Worlds; IVF: inverted file; SCT: Schema Conversion Tool; DMS: Database Migration Service; EMR: Elastic MapReduce

  • What the DEA-C01 exam asks, how it is scored and how to book it
  • The four domains, their weights and the 17 task statements that this course follows
  • The kind of question to expect: a data requirement, and the service or setting that fits it best
  • How the course is built: summaries, a running case, figures, exam tips and practice questions
  • A study plan and the ground rules for using official sources

2The Exam at a Glance

The numbers [Verify live]

Item Fact
Questions 65: 50 scored and 15 unscored (the unscored ones are not marked)
Time 130 minutes (about 2 minutes a question)
Result A scaled score from 100 to 1,000; 720 passes; the result is pass or fail
Scoring model Compensatory: you pass the exam as a whole, not each section
Unanswered Counted as wrong; there is no penalty for guessing
Fee and format USD 150; Pearson VUE test center or online proctored; valid 3 years (as of 7 November 2026)
Exam tip

Never leave a question blank: a guess costs nothing and a blank always scores zero.

Two kinds of question

  • Multiple choice: one correct answer and three distractors
  • Multiple response: two or more correct answers out of five or more options; the question says how many to select
  • Distractors are plausible: services that are real and sometimes useful, but not the best fit for the stated requirement
Exam tip

On multiple response, every correct option must be chosen and no wrong one; read the count in the question ("Select TWO") before you read the options.

Who the exam is for

The guide describes a candidate with 2 to 3 years of data engineering experience and 1 to 2 years of hands-on AWS experience. The exam validates that you can implement data pipelines and monitor, troubleshoot and optimize their cost and performance by best practices.

Out of scope for the candidate (so not tested): performing ML training and inference, language-specific syntax, and drawing business conclusions from data.

Exam tip

Questions are about choosing and configuring AWS services for a data requirement, not about writing code. Learn what each service is for, what makes it fit, and what makes it a wrong answer.

3Four Domains, Seventeen Task Statements

Domain Weight Task statements
1 Data Ingestion and Transformation 34% 1.1 Perform data ingestion · 1.2 Transform and process data · 1.3 Orchestrate data pipelines · 1.4 Apply programming concepts
2 Data Store Management 26% 2.1 Choose a data store · 2.2 Understand data cataloging systems · 2.3 Manage the lifecycle of data · 2.4 Design data models and schema evolution
3 Data Operations and Support 22% 3.1 Automate data processing · 3.2 Analyze data · 3.3 Maintain and monitor data pipelines · 3.4 Ensure data quality
4 Data Security and Governance 18% 4.1 Apply authentication mechanisms · 4.2 Apply authorization mechanisms · 4.3 Ensure data encryption and masking · 4.4 Prepare logs for audit · 4.5 Understand data privacy and governance
  • The guide lists 120 skills under the 17 task statements; this course covers every one of them and nothing else
  • Domain 1 is the biggest: about one question in three is about ingesting, transforming, orchestrating or coding a pipeline
  • The guide is not exhaustive and is updated; AWS publishes changes about one month before the exam reflects them
Exam tip

Spend time in proportion to the weights, but do not skip the small domain: security and governance questions are short and often decided by one setting.

What changed in guide version 1.1 [Dates]

  • Published 12 December 2025; the older knowledge and skills lists were merged into one list of skills per task
  • New skills: integrating large language models (LLMs) for data processing, open table formats such as Apache Iceberg, vector index types (HNSW, IVF) and vectorization, business data catalogs in Amazon SageMaker Catalog, SageMaker Unified Studio domains and projects, and governance frameworks and data sharing patterns
  • Services added to the in-scope list: Amazon Aurora, Amazon Q, Amazon Bedrock, Amazon Kendra, AWS Data Exchange and Amazon S3 Tables; removed: AWS Cloud9, AWS CodeCommit and AWS Schema Conversion Tool as listed services (the skill list still names AWS SCT and AWS DMS Schema Conversion)
Exam tip

Older study material may miss the vector, Iceberg, LLM and SageMaker Catalog topics. They are in this course because they are in the current guide.

4How This Course Works

  • Modules 1 to 18 follow the exam guide: one module per task statement (task 1.1 has two)
  • Module 19 is a quick reference with a service chooser; module 20 covers exam technique and a final week
  • Every content module has: what you will learn, a Kestrel Freight case, the content with tables and figures, exam tips, practice questions with explanations, and a quick reference card
  • Kestrel Freight is a fictional freight and logistics company; its truck telemetry, shipment orders and customer data grow into a data platform, one decision per module. It is fictional and not a real company
Running case

Meet Kestrel Freight

  • Trucks send position and temperature readings every few seconds
  • Warehouses drop order files into storage every night
  • Customers expect live tracking and correct invoices
  • Auditors expect to know who saw which data
  • Your job: build the pipeline, one decision at a time

Labels you will see

  • [Verify live]: AWS changes this often; the item carries an "As of" date, and you should read the AWS page before you rely on it
  • Old name: a service or feature has a new name, and older questions may use the old one (for example Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose is now Amazon Data Firehose)
  • Beyond the guide: taught for understanding, not named in the exam guide
  • [Dates]: a date that matters for the exam

5Study Plan and Ground Rules

  • Study one module, then do its questions; read the quick reference card last
  • Cover every task statement: the guide does not weight them separately
  • Compare look-alike services: most wrong answers are real services that fit a different requirement (for example Kinesis Data Streams and Amazon Data Firehose, Athena and Redshift, Glue and EMR)
  • Read the requirement words: near real time, lowest cost, least operational overhead, serverless, exactly once, schema-on-read decide the answer
  • Use the last week for the recap module, the service chooser and exam technique
  • Independence: this course is independent and educational; it is not affiliated with, endorsed or sponsored by Amazon Web Services, and it shows no AWS logos. The AWS exam guide and documentation outrank this course on every fact and rule
Exam tip

Before you book, read AWS's current exam guide and certification page; fees, languages and rules change.

6Exam Q&A

6.1 Practice questions (choose the best answer; some ask for two)

S1How many of the questions on the DEA-C01 exam count toward the score?

  • A65
  • B15
  • C50
  • D130
Show the answer

Answer: C. The exam has 65 questions, of which 50 are scored and 15 are unscored; the unscored ones are not identified.

S2A candidate is unsure of the answer to a question and has no time left to think about it. What is the best action?

  • ALeave it blank, because wrong answers lose points
  • BSkip the whole section, because each section must be passed
  • CGuess, because there is no penalty for guessing
  • DFlag the question and never return to it
Show the answer

Answer: C. Unanswered questions are scored as incorrect and there is no penalty for guessing, so a guess can only help.

S3Which TWO statements about the DEA-C01 exam are correct? (Select TWO.)

  • AA candidate must reach a passing score in every domain
  • BThe exam includes performing machine learning training
  • CThe exam is scored on a scale of 100 to 1,000 and 720 is needed to pass
  • DMultiple response questions have two or more correct answers
  • EThe exam tests language-specific programming syntax
Show the answer

Answer: C, D. The scaled score runs from 100 to 1,000 with 720 to pass, and multiple response questions have two or more correct answers. Scoring is compensatory (no per-domain pass mark), and language syntax and ML training are out of scope.

S4Which domain carries the largest share of the scored content?

  • AData Store Management and Modeling
  • BData Security and Governance controls
  • CData Ingestion and Transformation
  • DData Operations and Support tasks
Show the answer

Answer: C. Domain 1, Data Ingestion and Transformation, is 34 percent of the scored content.

7Quick Reference Card

Topic Key fact
Exam 65 questions (50 scored, 15 unscored), 130 minutes, 720 of 1,000 to pass, multiple choice and multiple response
Scoring Compensatory; blank is wrong; guess when unsure
Domains Ingestion and Transformation 34%, Data Store Management 26%, Operations and Support 22%, Security and Governance 18%
Task statements 17, with 120 skills; this course covers each once
Guide version 1.1, 12 December 2025: adds LLMs, vectors, Iceberg, SageMaker Catalog
Out of scope ML training and inference, language syntax, business conclusions
Method Read the requirement words; compare look-alike services; trust AWS documentation over any course
